messages.subject: Troubleshooting for large confidence intervals
parts:
Hello Group,

We are working with barn owl movement data from birds tracked in agricultural lands. We’ve run an RSF analysis with rsf.fit() and are trying to understand why we keep getting very large confidence intervals for some landcover types (see figure attached for example). The birds tracked in this study breed in vineyard, orchard, forage and row crop habitats, and  landcover types were simplified from a USDA CropScape public raster layer. Any insights on where to begin troubleshooting or addressing the large confidence intervals would be very much appreciated.

Thanks,

Ryan

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Troubleshooting for large confidence intervals
parts:
Hi Ryan,

Did you feed in these data with raster::as.factor() to make sure that they are treated properly as categorical data with a reference category? If you include all categories as separate predictors, then their linear dependence yields infinite confidence intervals. Similarly, if there are some rarely used categories, then you get very large CIs, because the predictors become almost linearly dependent. What are the effective sample sizes of the home-range estimates and what proportion of each individual dataset falls into all of these categories?

Best,
Chris
